t19: The hard part of running a raffle isn't picking the winner; it's making participants trust the result. In a good raffle, how someone won should be as visible as who won. Below is an end-to-end method that works.
t20: 1. Write rules clearly in the announcement
t21: Most post-raffle arguments come from rules that weren't written upfront. Put these in your announcement:
t24: How many people will win and how many backups will be drawn.
t25: How the winner will be announced and how long they have to respond.
t26: Whether writing multiple comments gives more chances.
t28: The cleaner the list, the less disputed the raffle. The same person appearing multiple times causes later "how did this person win" questions.
t29: Remove duplicate names (unless your rules say otherwise).
t30: Don't add people who didn't meet the requirements.
t31: Screenshot the list before the raffle.
t33: Picking the winner by hand creates doubt even if the choice really is random. Using a name picker both speeds things up and makes the result recordable.
t34: Recording the selection moment is the most powerful transparency tool: list visible, drawing visible, result visible.
t36: Many winners never respond to claim the prize. Picking at least one backup for each prize prevents having to run the raffle again. Explain the backup order upfront: "If 1st backup doesn't respond within 48 hours, 2nd backup is chosen."
t37: 5. Announce the result in the same place
t38: Explain the winner on the post or story where the raffle was announced.
t40: Write when and how the prize will be delivered.
t41: Thank everyone who entered; next raffle's participation depends on this.
t42: Multiple raffle types in one app
t43: Quick Raffle brings together a name picker, number draw, spinner, bag, team picker, dice, coin flip, card draw, and list shuffle in one place. You can paste a participant list and pick winners and backups all on one screen.
t45: How many backups should I draw in a raffle?
t46: At least one per prize is recommended. In raffles with high participation, picking two backups greatly reduces the risk of an unclaimed prize.
t47: Can the same person enter multiple times?
t48: That's entirely your rule; what matters is stating it clearly in the announcement. Any rule you don't write becomes a debate when the result drops.
t49: How do I show a raffle is fair?
t50: Screenshot the participant list before the drawing and share the selection moment with a screen recording. A visible process is the strongest transparency tool.
